analysis: Pseudotumour cerebri, also known as idiopathic intracranial hypertension, is a condition characterized by increased intracranial pressure without an identifiable cause. Among the listed drugs, Tetracycline is well-documented to be associated with this condition due to its potential to increase intracranial pressure. The other options, Sparfloxacin, Gentamicin, and Clofazimine, do not have established links to Pseudotumour cerebri in the medical literature. Therefore, based on the consensus and known pharmacological effects, Tetracycline is the most likely drug to cause Pseudotumour cerebri.
